subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit soft-steer lifecycle that interrupts or pauses active generation/tool work, injects user input, and resumes with partial context, or keep steering as boundary-based delivery plus separate interrupt mode?
rationale: The choice affects shared runtime semantics, user-visible channel behavior, Codex/native runtime integration, fallback behavior, and compatibility with existing steer/followup/interrupt modes.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering
options.body: Document current steer semantics as the supported default and use narrower PRs only to ensure messages reach the existing boundary-based policy.

options.title: Broaden Default Steer
options.body: Change default steer to stronger soft-steer semantics only after explicit upgrade proof and channel/runtime compatibility coverage.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
recommendation.body: Add a separate mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the focused replacement PR for active non-streaming steering and are the strongest available owner for the shared active-run lifecycle tradeoff.
